S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation, is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by persistent, impairing patterns of motor restlessness, excessive talking, difficulty remaining seated or quiet, and impulsive interruption across settings. In adults, it may be partially compensated for by structured routines or activity-heavy work until a life change exposes the impairment; it is distinguished from mania, anxiety, or situational stress by its non-episodic course, longstanding pattern, and absence of a primary mood or fear syndrome.

patient.stressor_event: Son or daughter leaving home (marriage, attending college, joined military)
patient.stressor: After Idalmis’s youngest child left South Carolina to attend college, she filled the quiet evenings with extra Spanish-department projects, cultural-center workshops, softball, book club, and food preparation for community events. Across the next 8 months, the new empty-nest schedule revealed a restlessness she had previously absorbed through parenting duties and rigid planning, with increasing difficulty remaining seated in faculty meetings, staying quiet during shared activities, and waiting her turn in group discussions. The impairment was noticeable but contained: colleagues teased her about pacing during curriculum meetings, her book club complained that she interrupted too often, and her husband noticed that she seemed constantly in motion during evenings that were supposed to be restful. Idalmis requested an evaluation herself after a professional-development seminar on adult ADHD made her realize the pattern was persistent across school, home, and community settings.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: When I'm sitting at my desk grading essays or in church, I catch myself tapping my foot, clicking my pen, or shifting around so much that I have to remind myself to settle down.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: What brought me in is that I keep getting up in meetings or at dinner when everyone else is seated, like I'll suddenly need to refill coffee, check a handout, or walk to the back of the room even though nothing is really urgent.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: At book club or during quiet evenings with my husband, I have a hard time just sitting quietly with the book or the movie, and before I know it I'm commenting, rustling in the kitchen, or suggesting we do something else.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: Since the house got quieter after my youngest left for college, I move from lesson planning to laundry to softball practice to chopping food for a community event without much pause, even on nights I promised myself I would rest.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: I notice I can take over a conversation in the Spanish department or at the cultural center, giving three examples when one would do, and then I feel embarrassed when I see people trying to wrap it up.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: In group discussions I often jump in before someone has finished their thought, especially at book club or curriculum meetings, because the response is already in my head and I blurt it out before I can stop myself.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_age_12_years: Even as a girl, my report cards said I was bright but could not stay in my seat or wait my turn, and my mother used to joke that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: It has started to affect my relationships at work and in my community because people lose patience with me in meetings and book club, and I leave feeling embarrassed instead of connected.
add_requirements.duration: This has been noticeably harder to manage for about eight months, since my youngest left for college and the house became quieter.
